newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign funds help Bombay shares close steady.
newsitem.headline: Foreign funds help Bombay shares close steady.

text.p: Share prices finished little changed at Bombay bourses on Friday after an early slide prompted a flurry of foreign institutional demand, brokers said.
"The FIIs (foreign institutional investors) steadied the market," said Vijay Pandya, a director at Classic Share and Stock Brokers. "They bought a range of index-linked shares."
The last day of weekly account at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) pulled prices down at the start and fresh demand was discouraged by three-day weekend holiday, traders said.
The 30-share BSE index closed 2.58 points higher at a provisional 3,405.18 after dropping to 3,377.22.
The BSE is closed on Monday for a Moslem festival.
Traders said Bajaj Auto, ITC, Reliance, Colgate, BSES and Tata Hydro-Electric were some of shares bought by the FIIs.
Pandya said the foreign demand was prompted by overnight gains in the global depositary receipts of Indian firms listed and traded abroad.
Taking the cue some local players also turned buyers towards the close and the undercurrent was hopeful, dealers said.
"I don't see the market going down," said Rasesh Maniar, dealer at Mukesh Babu Securities Ltd. "Budget expectations will keep prices up."
Indian finance minister P Chidambaram is scheduled to present the annual budget on February 28.
The 50-share National Stock Exchange (NSE) index gained 9.50 points to a provisional 977.25.
The NSE said it will be open on Monday for trading, but banks, government offices, companies and most commodity markets are closed for a Moslem festival.
At the BSE, ITC rose 14.50 rupees 398.75, Cadbury 9.0 to 345, Colgate 6.25 to 275.50, BSES 3.25 to 232, BHEL 3.75 to 221, Castrol 4.25 to 435, Tata Tea 10 to 233.50. Hind Lever fell 8.50 to 885.
